raw_segments.text: Chorus, Ahwoe, and Welladee, I would that fate, not bearing agony too great, nor stretching
me too long on couch of pain, Would bid mine eyelids keep the morningless
For life is weary, now my lord is slain, The gracious among kings.
Hard fate of old he bore and many grievous things,
And for a woman's sake on Illian land, Now is his life hewn down and by a woman's
O Helen, O infatuate soul, Who bads tee the tides of battle roll,
Or whelming thousands, life on life, Neath Illian's wall,
And now lies dead the lord of all.
The blossom of thy storied sin Bears blood's inexpeable stain.
O thou that erst, these halls within, Word unto all a rock of strife,
